title: Shift sampling decision to ingress proxy to eliminate hot-path SDK span overhead
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Problem: SDKs currently create full span objects for nearly every RPC and HTTP request. For high-throughput services this generates excessive CPU, memory churn, and telemetry traffic even for spans that will later be discarded by sampling. We observe elevated p95 latency and increased GC pauses in frontend pods during peak traffic (linked in comments).

Proposed solution: move the initial sampling decision into the ingress layer (Envoy / edge proxy) so the majority of low-value requests never materialize heavy span objects inside service processes. The ingress will run a lightweight per-request evaluator that sets a sampling-decision header (redwood-trace-sample: accept|reject|defer). Service SDKs will consult this header and either skip full span allocation, emit minimal breadcrumb metrics, or mark the trace ID for deferred tail evaluation. This reduces hot-path overhead while preserving tail-based detection and per-customer budgets.

Key design points:
- Deterministic hashing: use request attributes (customer_id cookie or header + trace-id) hashed at ingress to provide sticky reservoir sampling.
- Route-level budgets: envoy config supports per-route budget tokens to respect SLA tiers and prevent token exhaustion.
- Defer flow: for flows that require tail-based analysis, ingress can mark as "defer" and carry a lightweight marker; services will capture only minimal KV-cache tokens to enable later rehydration if the trace is selected.
- Backward compatibility: if the header is absent (older proxies or direct traffic), SDKs fall back to existing client-side sampling.
- Telemetry: add ingress metrics (decisions/sec, accepted%, deferred%, CPU delta) and correlate with service-level span/sec and latency.

Rollout plan:
1) Build Envoy filter prototype in feature branch; unit tests and integration harness.
2) Ship to internal staging for two canary services (auth and upload). Monitor span/sec, p50/p95 latency, heap allocs, GC frequency.
3) Gradual rollout across edge cluster with per-route enablement flags.
4) Enable per-customer quotas and give customers an opt-in toggle via Console.

Acceptance criteria:
- 50% reduction in SDK-created span objects for canary services under normal workload.
- No regression (>5% increase) in p95 latency for user-facing routes.
- Defer path rehydration correctness validated end-to-end in trace replay tests.

Security considerations: sampling decision header must be authenticated/immutable between ingress and downstream; use mTLS or signed header tokens to prevent spoofing. Security review required before production rollout.
